prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
'adoption, redesign' changes have shown helpful, positive results after noise correction across 2 tests, backed by a winning test.
'adoption, new_flow' changes have shown no clear effect across 3 tests.
'sign_in, redesign' changes have shown negative results after noise correction across 2 tests.
Evidence is still thin for 'finish, new_screen', 'finish, redesign', and 'sign_in, reorder' changes, as their tests either lack a second trial or disagree on effect.
Predictions have mostly been too high compared to noise-corrected measurements, though rounds 7, 8, 9, 12, and 13 were underestimated.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, new_flow: -0.7% after noise correction, 3 test(s)
- adoption, redesign: +5.9% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- finish, new_screen: +0.1% after noise correction, 3 test(s)
- finish, redesign: -2.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, redesign: -3.8% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- sign_in, reorder: -6.9% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 68.4%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 20.0%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [finish, redesign] home_intro_spotlight_redesign: Redesign the finish onboarding screen into a spotlight layout that highlights essential controls and desktop pet interaction steps. (why: Finish screen drop-off is high (64.8% conversion) with a mean time of 5815s, and support logs show confusion on controlling or finding the pet.)
1: [home, new_screen] new_waiting_progress_companion_screen: Insert a dedicated waiting companion screen that displays an animated preparation process while the desktop pet is generated. (why: The waiting step has a median duration of 201s and mean of 2336s, leading to drop-offs while assets load.)
2: [sign_in, reorder] sign_in_reorder_after_adoption: Reorder the onboarding flow so that sign-in happens after pet adoption selection instead of before. (why: Sign-in drops 27.1% of users before they get to choose a pet, creating unnecessary early friction.)
3: [adoption, hint] upload_photos_file_format_hint: Add an explicit photo formatting hint to the photo upload screen explaining lighting and background requirements. (why: Support logs show 3 user reports of custom pet creation failing or looking wrong during photo upload.)
4: [home, wait_info] waiting_time_estimate_display: Display a visible step counter and estimated time remaining during the pet creation waiting phase. (why: Users spend up to 2336s on average on the waiting step without feedback on how long rendering will take.)
5: [finish, copy] home_intro_desktop_visibility_copy: Update final screen headlines and text to explicitly explain where the pet appears on the desktop and taskbar. (why: Multiple support emails reported pets not showing on desktop or users being unable to open the desktop pet.)
6: [home, notification] waiting_ready_desktop_notification: Enable optional system notifications on the waiting screen to alert users when pet setup completes. (why: High average waiting times cause users to switch away to other apps and drop off before finishing.)
7: [sign_in, layout] sign_in_compact_layout_view: Switch sign-in screen to a compact layout emphasizing account continuity and existing user account syncing. (why: 8 support emails complained about pets missing or reset after signing in with a different or duplicate account.)

scores.note: Finish step has highest drop-off (35.2%) and strong support evidence, but screen redesigns here previously measured -2.1%.
Addresses high wait time on home step, but adding new screens/flows has consistently shown weak or neutral results.
Sign-in has 27.1% drop-off, but reordering sign-in previously resulted in a significant -6.9% drop.
Adoption step drops 31.6%; simple copy/hint additions on adoption steps carry low risk and high confidence.
Home step has lower drop-off (18.7%), but adding time estimates addresses extreme wait times at config-only cost.
Finish step has highest drop-off and strong support complaint volume; copy clarification is low cost and high leverage.
Helps re-engage users during long 2336s wait times, though target step drop-off is relatively low.
Strong support evidence (8 emails), but past sign_in redesigns consistently showed negative lift (-3.8%).
